post.title: Numbers from my first 3-month Steam game (700 wishlists, $2,123 gross) and why a small genre event beat Next Fest by 3x
post.author: mrnovembeer
post.text:
I shipped my first commercial game called Immunica a few months ago after 3 months of solo dev. It's a small Nodebuster style incremental game.
 I did almost zero marketing during development (literally 3 shorts and a few tweets) and was sitting at 82 wishlists a month before Next Fest.
 Here is how the numbers ended up looking:
 Tiny Roguelikes event: +474 wishlists in 2 weeks
 Steam Next Fest: +160 wishlists
 Wishlists at launch: ~700
 Sales: 147 in the first 3 days, 234 first week, 895 total so far
 Revenue: $2,123 gross (~$1,100 net after Steam cut, taxes, refunds)
 Outstanding Wishlist: 1,081
 Biggest surprise for me was Next Fest vs smaller festivals. If you go into Next Fest with ~500 wishlists, you just get buried. Niche genre events convert way better when you're small.
 Also a random tip: manually check your Polish pricing on Steam. Steam's default PLN conversion is super high right now. There's a PolishOurPrices movement in Poland and they pointed it out to me on Twitter during launch week, I lowered it, and some posts about it just went viral there. Poland ended up being my #1 market (201 copies sold).
 Anyway, I teamed up with an artist friend for my next incremental game Feed The Pond so it doesn't have my programmer art this time, and we put the Steam page up early instead of waiting until the last minute.
 Made a quick 5 min video breaking down the launch graphs and showing the new game if anyone wants to check it out: Video
